paragraphs.name: Situation
paragraphs.plain: Where the trope system stands: what Chief asked on 9/29, what existed before, and how far the register has grown.

strand.last: The plot system had a trope graph, but it covered only the Plot indexes of TV Tropes. Character, setting, theme, genre and sexuality had no trope layer at all.
strand.plan: Build one trope register that every system can key into, fetched by script from TV Tropes, keyed by specialists in batches, and checked by a script at the end of each batch.
strand.you: You asked on 9/29 for one trope layer across everything, ruled all four recs, and have since said go on each wave. On 10/03 you ordered BOLO 89 "all approved running".
strand.next: Wave B (theme and style) finishes fetching, then gets keyed and checked.

items.t: "do we have one for tropes in general to apply through all of these? … a whole one for tropes using TV Tropes … overall, so it's able to be applied for everything like sexuality."

"I'll recommend" — all four recs ruled: the register lives in 01 NARRATIVE_FRAMEWORKS · each trope carries its name, a one-line definition and a `domains:` list · the tropes are fetched by script · keying runs in the BOLO 77 formation.

"all recommendations" — the keying call: each trope keys to a layer of its own domain's slice (character L1–L12 · setting S1–S12 · genre G1–G12 · sexuality onto the character layers · theme onto the four rails R1–R4, or null).
"Recommendations" — the theme sub-index pass (Death · Family · Betrayal · Revenge · Authority · Memory · The Secret · Promises and Vows).
"can we do more development and more pulls on tvtropes.com" — a second probe of candidate indexes, then all recs ruled.
"get BOLO 89 all approved running" (10/03) — wave A keyed and wave B fetching.
The plot trope graph (`ssot_04_trope_graph.md`, v0.1.3) keys 1,034 TV Tropes tropes, but only from the Plot indexes, onto 135 plot nodes.
The register `01_NARRATIVE_FRAMEWORKS/📐 ssot_01_trope_register.md` is at v0.4.0 with 7,070 keyed tropes; its data is `_tools/tropes/data/domains/register.json` and its pull list is `LAYERS.md`.
TROPES sections were added to the character, genre, theme and setting systems.
Public-repo rule stands: names and one-line definitions only.

Index probe 9/29: character = CharactersAsDevice 1,447 + CharacterizationTropes 122 + ArchetypalCharacter 104 · setting = Settings 650 · genre = Genres 79 + GenreTropes 26 · sexuality = SexTropes 441 · theme = TopicalTropes, an index of indexes. About 3,000 tropes before de-duplication.

Fetch 9/29: 3,094 unique tropes (character 1,624 · setting 643 · sexuality 445 · theme 326 · genre 105; 49 in more than one domain; 97 overlap the plot pull). 3,093 of 3,094 links fetched. Theme was thin because Death, Family, Betrayal and Revenge list sub-indexes, not tropes, and FateAndProphecy returns 404.
Register v0.1.0 (9/29): 3,094 keyed (high 2,193 · medium 243 · low 658); the script reviewer found 5 problems, all fixed to 0.
Theme pass (9/29): register v0.2.0 at 4,948 tropes; theme R1 274 · R2 560 · R3 321 · R4 386 · null 797.
Low-confidence pass (9/29): 952 definitions fetched and re-keyed; register v0.3.0 (high 3,919 · medium 797 · low 232); character nulls fell from 348 to 94.

Probe 9/29 (`_tools/tropes/probe.py`) ran 60 candidate indexes and found about 4,000 tropes new to the register: texture, time, OXO settings (religion, school, cyberpunk, vehicles, drugs), war, theme (love, power, identity, emotion) and style.

Wave A keyed 10/03: 2,122 tropes on 12 batches, script check at 0 after fixes. The first pass put 797 setting tropes on S1 and 336 texture tropes on T7; the fan-in caught it and they were re-keyed (S1 now 366 · T7 25 · texture null 318, which are plot-content tropes the index carries).
Open: 380 tropes with no definition, and wiring the plot trope graph as a consumer of the register.

paragraphs.name: Mission
paragraphs.plain: A mission is a task plus the reason for it. This one's reason: the plot system had tropes, but character, setting, theme, genre, sexuality, texture and tracking had none, so no layer could pull a known pattern.

strand.last: Wave A keyed on 10/3: 2,122 new tropes, re-keyed twice after the first pass dumped them on two default layers.
strand.plan: One register in 01 that every system keys into; fetch by script, key by Payload Specialists, check by RANGE the script.
strand.you: You said "get BOLO 89 all approved running" on 10/3. Wave A landed; wave B is fetching.
strand.next: Wave B fetch finishes, then keying for theme and style, then RANGE and register v0.5.0.

paragraphs.task: Build one cross-domain trope register under every system,
paragraphs.intent: in order to give every layer of every system (character, setting, genre, sexuality, theme, texture, tracking, style) a keyed pull list of known patterns, with the plot trope graph as the first consumer.
paragraphs.spoken: "Do we have one for tropes in general to apply through all of these? … a whole one for tropes using TV Tropes … overall, so it's able to be applied for everything like sexuality." · "Can we do more development and more pulls on tvtropes.com" · "Get BOLO 89 all approved running."
endstate: One register (`register.json` + `LAYERS.md`): every trope with name, one-line definition, domains, one key per domain, and confidence.
Every system's TROPES section points at its own layer list.
Waves A and B keyed and RANGE-clean; no default-dumping on a single layer.
Names and one-line definitions only, never page text (the repo is public).

strand.plan: Wave B pulls the theme and style indexes at one request a second, then specialists key them in batches and the script checks the result.

strand.next: Wave B finishes fetching; keying and the check follow.

paragraphs.main_effort: Wave B: fetch, then key, the theme and style tropes.

phases.t: **Rulings and fetch.** Four recs ruled; `fetch.py --domains` pulled 3,094 tropes into `_tools/tropes/data/domains/` (3,093 of 3,094 links).
**First keying and register v0.1.0.** 16 batches of about 194, three specialists on disjoint batches, script check `_tools/bolostatus/work/89/range.py`; 3,094 keyed, 5 findings fixed to 0.
**Theme sub-index pass, register v0.2.0.** 4,948 tropes; 2,012 needed a theme key, in 9 batches (T1–T9) with two specialists keying; TROPES sections added to character, genre, theme and setting.
**Low-confidence second pass, register v0.3.0.** 952 definitions fetched with `fetch_defs.py` and re-keyed (R1–R6); script check 0.

**Probe of 60 more indexes.** `_tools/tropes/probe.py` found about 4,000 new tropes; all recs ruled; seeds added to `fetch.py` and new domains to `build_register.py` (texture T1–T12 · tracking world_clock/told_order/grid/story_point/cable/tempo · style 06.1/06.3).
**Wave A keyed.** 2,122 tropes on 12 batches; script check 0 after fixes; the S1 and T7 pile-ups re-keyed (AR1–AR6, then AT1); register v0.4.0, 7,070 keyed.

**Wave B fetching.** Love · Power · Emotion · Identity (theme) plus Language · Costume · Graphical · Lighting · Amazing Technicolor (style): 1,632 tropes at 1 request a second; keying runs behind the fetch.

**Close the open items.** Definitions for the 380 tropes that have none, and the plot trope graph wired as a consumer of the register. The 292 plot tropes held from BOLO 77 are re-keyed in the same run.

running: Wave B fetch of 1,632 theme and style tropes at 1 request a second; keying behind it.

items.t: **ACTUAL**: scope, which TV Tropes indexes join, what a domain means. **Claude**: the fetch, the keys, the checks; adds no trope the index does not list.

**RANGE is a script.** `_tools/bolostatus/work/89/range.py` checks every keys file against its batch: each slug once, a legal key per domain, a legal confidence. A spread check (no layer swallowing a domain) is done by the main line at the fan-in.
Register doc version bumps on every keyed wave; BOLO row 89 carries the status; this sheet takes FRAGOs.
